scope: Read-only reassessment against actual server and client policy; no edits/tests/launches, foreign raw evidence or issue execution inspected. Only this report written.
correctionToPriorReview: The prior statement that native output-only401/403 should preserve the chat/draft was unsupported. Bypassing the callback is the current implementation, not an established intentional policy. This review supersedes that semantic conclusion.
decision: A concrete native invalidation-path gap exists: authoritative401/403 from a validated lazy output read does not reach the adopted6487 conversation purge callback. Add a fail-first AppModel/URLProtocol regression and reuse the shared denial helper. No legitimate finer-grained output403 policy was found.

establishedEvidence.finding: The read handler returns400 for invalid references,200 for admitted output,409 for ambiguity and404 for unavailable/withheld output. It has no401/403 branch or output-specific authorization policy.
Raw requests pass deviceAccess.handle before Next handles the route.
Managed-device tailnet/approval/credential gates can refuse the API request with403 before the handler. These apply to desktop access, not a per-tool output capability.

Global API host/origin/credential policy applies to this request; invalid access can return401/403. Not every such response proves durable revocation, but no narrow output-only grant or403 exception was found.
Web lazy output explicitly invalidatesChatAccess for the requested session on401/403. It does not invalidate on404.
Web invalidation evicts conversation state and advances its generation; full conversation reads use the same401/403 denial policy.
Access invalidation clears admitted turns/context/failed-send carry and aborts the live owner. This is broader than an output-card error.
The adopted native conversation-read policy invokes the optional denial callback for401/403;404/5xx do not purge.

Lazy read checks cancellation then maps401/403 to ToolOutputError.unauthorized without invoking that callback. Therefore this request alone leaves AppModel revoked sets/held object/draft mirror and persisted snapshots uninformed.
The shared callback is connection/generation-bound and performs held-object/memory/draft-mirror invalidation plus uncancellable selective disk purge. Reusing it preserves those fences.

minimalRepairRecommendation: First add tool-output to the real AppModel/URLProtocol operation table, expecting ToolOutputError.unauthorized and selective disk removal. Current nine-operation table omits this path. Assert affected held memory/draft mirror cannot revive and unrelated snapshot remains unchanged; reproduce before implementation.

Make purgeConversationIfAccessDenied module-internal so CaveClient+ToolOutput.swift can reuse it; keep callback storage private. Invoke it only after validating HTTP response identity against the exact requested URL.

For a validated received401/403, await the shared purge before Task.checkCancellation can discard the denial. Existing6487 policy requires completed purge despite caller cancellation; merely inserting the callback after the current cancellation check leaves that gap.

Retain deferred task cancellation, strict same-endpoint/redirect checks, fixed error copy, no server-body exposure, byte-exact accepted data,2MiB envelope and256KiB UTF8 bounds. Do not read the denial body to decide whether this GET should purge.
Keep404 unavailable/withheld,409 ambiguity,400 invalid references,5xx/transport and local validation failures nonpurging. Known outputDisclosure=withheld continues to avoid the request entirely.
Do not alter sendStream403 classification: write-only project access, flow-read-only and harness refusals remain nonpurging; only its existing conversation-access/managed-device categories purge.
verificationNeededNotPerformed: Fail-first tool-output403 in ThreadSnapshotStoreTests.testConversationSpecificRequestsPurgeTheirRefusedSession, then green after shared-helper reuse. Catch its specific ToolOutputError without weakening existing CaveError checks or selective-cache assertions.
Add/extend status boundaries for tool-output401/403 versus404/409/5xx; verify callback generation replacement and received-denial cancellation semantics through the shared AppModel path.
Keep direct-client ToolOutputTests unauthorized-message/no-body/no-retry assertions. They currently use callback nil and do not establish AppModel invalidation.
Run relevant native/store/transport contracts after implementation; current canonical green source evidence does not cover a change not yet made.

possibleUIEffects.currentUITest: AgentActivityUITests.testDeniedToolOutputNeverShowsServerErrorBody currently expects the refusal sheet to remain and the same Show output row to be reopenable. With an AppModel-bound401/403 purge, thread/message scope clears and ChatView dismissal guards can dismiss that sheet and remove the owning row.
possibleUIEffects.testPolicy: Inspect and update that scenario to assert the stronger intended revocation behavior while retaining no-private-error-body/no-unauthorized-retry requirements. Do not merely accept either behavior. Preserve separate404/known-withheld tests proving no cache purge and no unnecessary lazy read.
possibleUIEffects.draftScope: 6487 clears the affected in-memory draft mirror; its README explicitly leaves user-authored composer preferences on their separate lifecycle. Do not broaden this repair into deleting all local drafts.
possibleUIEffects.historyFixture: The read-only history preview direct CaveClient has callback nil by design and remains outside AppModel revocation acceptance.

certainty: Server status distinctions, web invalidation and missing native callback are established by source inspection. Actual failing sentinel/UI behavior has not been executed in this review; proposed fail-first tests must supply runtime proof. No new server grant policy is inferred.
